A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from UniCoD to UniJEPA. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original CALVIN and SimplerEnv evaluations, experiments on two physical robot platforms, ablations, and qualitative representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds a real-world XArm pretraining ablation in Table 5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 replace the λ1- and λ2-weighted training objectives with unweighted sums of their constituent losses. This revises the stated objectives; whether implementation changed is unspecified. The architecture, two-stage training procedure, and action-generation mechanism otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The pretraining datasets in v1 Table 8 and v3 Table 9 match. CALVIN, SimplerEnv, Franka, and XArm coverage is retained, including seen and unseen conditions. The new XArm ablation uses already represented manipulation tasks.

E2.justification: The simulation comparator sets are substantially revised. Both SimplerEnv comparisons replace OpenVLA with OpenVLA-OFT and add π0-Fast and GR00T-N1.5; the WidowX comparison removes SpatialVLA. The CALVIN table removes RT-1 and π0 while retaining GR-1, VPP, and UP-VLA.

E3.justification: The new XArm ablation introduces full-pretraining, no-pretraining, and no-discrete-pretraining controls. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, image settings, and action chunks are retained. The main-text change from 20 to 20/50 trials matches counts already documented in v1 Appendix A.3, rather than establishing increased sampling.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 adds a focused real-world test of overall and discrete pretraining on pick-and-place, cup relocation, and unseen pick-and-place. The existing simulation ablations, appendix t-SNE analysis, and OOD demonstrations remain.

E5.justification: v3 Section 4.3 and Tables 7–8 newly specify averaging over three checkpoints and describe error bars as checkpoint variance. v1 does not specify this checkpoint count. This is new reporting, not evidence of increased runs; the claimed error bars are not visibly present in Figures 4–5.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for the revised simulation comparators and the XArm ablation, whose reported averages are 76.7, 60.8, and 71.7 for full, no, and no-discrete pretraining. CALVIN's RT-1 and π0 numerical rows disappear. The proposed method's main reported scores remain 4.11 on CALVIN and 71.0/78.4 on SimplerEnv, with the principal real-world results also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of the combined losses change: v1 Equations 1 and 3 contain adjustable relative weights, whereas v3 Sections 3.1–3.2 give unit-weight combinations. The remaining mathematical formulation is retained, and neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified discrete and continuous representations, two-stage training, generalization, and leading performance. The introduction's added 12% dexterous-hand statement elaborates a gain already claimed in v1's abstract.

C2.justification: v3 Section 3.3 newly asserts that additional experts increase only pretraining overhead without increasing inference latency; no timing evidence accompanies this assertion. Existing explanations concerning feature alignment, initialization, and generalization remain, without substantive new limitations.

D1.justification: v3 discloses 2.9B total parameters, divided into a 2.3B VLM and two 0.3B experts, and adds comparator model sizes to the WidowX table. It removes v1's explicit identification of open-pi-zero as the π0 implementation. Most training and data-processing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to GR00T N1, DreamVLA, and VLM4VLA, and replaces the Qwen2.5-VL reference with Qwen3-VL. These update the literature coverage while retaining the central positioning against discrete-token visual prediction approaches.

P1.justification: The method is renamed throughout, headings and selected paragraphs are edited, and the pretraining discussion moves within the ablation section. The manuscript-polishing disclosure in v1 Appendix B is removed. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main paper is extensively reformatted into two columns, with resized and relocated figures and tables. v3 adds an ablation table and a model-size column, and separates appendix displays onto additional float pages. The environment overview Figure 3 disappears, leaving a Figure ?? reference. The XArm table drops OpenVLA rows although Figure 5 retains that comparator.

improvement.justification: The XArm ablation, updated baselines, and parameter disclosures strengthen the evidence and documentation. However, v3 claims error bars absent from Figures 4–5 and retains a CALVIN comparison to π0 after deleting its numerical results. New Table 2 success averages are also inconsistent: OpenVLA-OFT's task-success entries average 15.6%, versus the reported 39.6%; π0-Fast's average 32.1%, versus 48.3%. These benefits and new reporting problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
